title: Threat as a Checkable Predicate: code and results
description:
Code and result artefacts for the paper Threat as a Checkable Predicate: What Anomaly-Based Web Detection Omits.

An anomaly-based intrusion detector reports that a request is unusual; what matters operationally is whether it is harmful. Public intrusion-detection corpora contain only ordinary traffic and attacks, with no legitimate-but-unusual category, so a detector's inability to separate the two is invisible under standard evaluation. This repository constructs the missing category from requests a corpus already labels normal, and measures separation: the rate at which a criterion fires on attacks minus the rate at which it fires on legitimate anomalies.

Contents: the probe generator and its validity guards, independent per-condition assessment of a formal threat predicate, faithful implementations of the Kruegel-Vigna character-distribution model and PAYL, a three-role multi-agent system, a threat relation graph, and the result artefacts backing every number reported in the paper.

Corpora are not redistributed; download instructions are in the README.
